metadata.title: Week 6 Progress
metadata.narration_policy: Narration is SCRIPT.md verbatim, one script section per beat: B00 = section 1, B01-B06 = sections 2-7, BOUT = section 8.
metadata.visual_policy: Simple illustrative Manim cards in the humanitarians palette, in the same style as the Week 3 progress video. No photos or recordings of the fellow, no person icons, no real company, product or tool logos. No Google, reCAPTCHA or Cloudflare logos and no screenshots of real challenge pages: a CAPTCHA is shown only as a plain drawn grid of squares, and Claude Code as a generic drawn terminal. Tools named in the narration are generic drawn shapes or plain text. Any file, terminal or video frame shown is drawn, not a screenshot. Every shape is an illustration of what the script says, not real data.
metadata.structure_note: Same structure as the Week 3 progress video: Claude composer cold open, six body cards, logo outro. No hesitant-writer, verdict or Your Turn beats, because the narration is the fellow's script exactly and the script has no lines for them.

portrait_layout.rule: In 9:16, all text and labels sit above 86% of the frame height (y < 0.86 * H), leaving the bottom 14% empty. Portrait text is at least 72 px at 2160x3840. Portrait type is large and labels are short.

metadata.fill_rule: Gate V needs content covering at least 55% of the safe area at 50% and at 85% of every beat. Each scene lays out its full cast early and holds it, and every scene is built to fill the frame.
metadata.gate_t_note: Gate T can read thin tick marks or outlines near text as letters. No thin ticks or outlines sit near text: dial ticks are pale and kept apart from labels, and cards that hold text use a soft border.
metadata.library_check: Searched with ./art scenes first: see SHOTLIST.md. Reused: ClaudeComposerAsk / ClaudeComposerAsk916 and LogoOutro / LogoOutro916; B01-B06 are custom Manim.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Keya, and this is my week six progress update for the Brutalist project, where I'm learning film as code. The voice you're hearing is an AI voice reading my script.

show.event: the ask types in under 'Hi, Keya'
three result lines land: week 6 progress, film as code deeper, checking every claim
the AI-voice disclosure is spoken while the answered composer holds

props.command: Help me share my week: the video I made, what I learned, and how I checked it.

beats.narration_text: This week's explainer is How Do Websites Know I'm Not a Robot? I researched CAPTCHAs on websites and in two research studies, and built the video with Claude Code. Everything in this update was new for me.

show.event: title card for the explainer, text only
researched CAPTCHAs: a drawn grid of picture squares, and two drawn research papers
built with Claude Code: a drawn terminal
everything was new for me: a star

shot.visual_intent: title card for the explainer, text only; a plain drawn grid of squares for CAPTCHAs on websites beside two drawn paper pages for the two studies; a drawn terminal for Claude Code; a star for 'new for me'. No logo, no real challenge page.

beats.narration_text: I went deeper into film as code this week, especially how landscape and vertical videos are built. The narration is the same, but the checks are not. For text size, a landscape video needs at least forty-one pixels, and a vertical video needs at least seventy-two.

show.event: film as code, deeper: angle brackets and a film frame
landscape and vertical: a wide drawn frame and a tall one
the narration is the same, the checks are not
text size: 41 for landscape, 72 for vertical

shot.visual_intent: angle brackets turning into a film frame; a wide frame and a tall frame side by side (stacked in portrait) with the same narration bar under both; the text-size floors 41 and 72 shown as big numbers, one under each frame.

beats.narration_text: For this video, I set myself a rule: nothing goes in unless it's checked against a source. Even then, the fact check flagged five things to fix, from lines that said more than the sources did to one source that couldn't be opened. Because every line pointed to a source, each one was easy to fix.

show.event: the rule: nothing goes in unless it's checked against a source
the fact check flagged five things to fix
every line pointed to a source, so each was easy to fix

shot.visual_intent: a claim card tied to a source card; five claim rows, each with a source tag, with all five marked as saying more than the source; then each one ticked once fixed against its source.

beats.narration_text: The text-size check surprised me. It flagged tick marks on a dial, because it read them as tiny letters. Making them a paler colour fixed it, without changing any words.

show.event: the text-size check surprised me
it flagged tick marks on a dial: read as tiny letters
a paler colour fixed it, no words changed

shot.visual_intent: a drawn dial with pale tick marks and a crimson ring marking what the check flagged; then the same dial with paler ticks and a tick mark; a plain bar of text lines marked 'same words'. Ticks are kept pale and away from any text.

beats.narration_text: My vertical verdict card was a numbered list, but one sentence was split across four numbers, so it read oddly. I rewrote it as four complete thoughts.

show.event: my vertical verdict card was a numbered list
one sentence split across four numbers, so it read oddly
rewritten as four complete thoughts

shot.visual_intent: a drawn card with a numbered list of four ragged fragments of one sentence; then the same card with four full-width complete lines, each ticked. Placeholder bars only, no verdict wording.

beats.narration_text: More and more websites check how I behave, and a check is only as good as what it measures. This week, I learned to check my videos the same way: every claim needs a source, and every frame needs a second look.

show.event: more and more websites check how I behave
a check is only as good as what it measures
every claim needs a source
every frame needs a second look

shot.visual_intent: a drawn page with a wavy cursor path watched by an eye; a check box pointing at what it measures; a claim tied to a source; a drawn video frame with an eye looking again.
